tech_stack.persistence_access: Spring Data R2DBC, Flyway migrations, embedded H2 for boot/test only

topology: modular monolith, hexagonal per module; one deployable, one composition root

modules.role: core; owns validation, reordering, append-only raw records and Event Revisions; publishes events
derived transient sliding-window buffer; consumes ingestion events by published contract only; broadcasts WindowedTelemetryBroadcast

layers: application (use cases, inbound/outbound ports, no framework)
infrastructure (R2DBC adapters, in-process event bus adapter, config)
interface (WebFlux controllers, event consumers; call application ports only)

integration.external -> Telemetry Ingestion & Valida: Conformist; interface-layer anti-corruption mapping of device payload to Telemetry Sample commands; boundary validation + VALIDATION_FAILED tagging + reactive backpressure at the entry point
integration.Telemetry Ingestion & Validation -> Tele: Customer-supplier; published events TelemetrySampleIngested, TelemetrySampleValidationFailed, TelemetryBackfillRevisionAppended via an outbound EventPublisher port (application, ingestion) and a consumer adapter in distribution; eventual consistency; distribution never reads raw storage
integration.Telemetry Stream Distribution -> externa: Open host service / published language WindowedTelemetryBroadcast; consumer demand signalling keeps broadcast non-blocking

build_order: T0 scaffold (pom.xml, single composition root, test profile, surefire timeout, Flyway runner)
shared kernel (event contracts: TelemetrySampleIngested, TelemetrySampleValidationFailed, TelemetryBackfillRevisionAppended, WindowedTelemetryBroadcast; correlation key)

surfaces.name: Ingress packet ingest HTTP inbound
operations: ingest Ingress Packet carrying Telemetry Samples
validate, reorder by t_device, append raw record or Event Revision
surfaces.traced_from: context-map: external -> Telemetry Ingestion & Validation (Conformist); actors IoT edge device, Bike computer, Smart wearable

surfaces.name: Ingestion events consumer
surfaces.traced_from: context-map: Telemetry Ingestion & Validation -> Telemetry Stream Distribution (Customer-supplier)

surfaces.name: Windowed telemetry stream HTTP outbound feed
operations: subscribe to WindowedTelemetryBroadcast as a backpressure-aware server-sent event stream
surfaces.traced_from: context-map: Telemetry Stream Distribution -> external (Open host service); actors Downstream streaming analytics consumers

rules.statement: Every Telemetry Sample is validated against its Sensor Metric Boundary (HR: 30-240 BPM, Power: 0-2500W, Cadence: 0-220 RPM, Swimming Pace: >45 sec/100m) before downstream propagation
Invalid samples are tagged VALIDATION_FAILED and the underlying payload is never dropped
Packets delayed up to 60 seconds are ordered by t_device, not t_ingress
Ingestion entry point applies reactive backpressure with zero blocking I/O on thread pools
Raw time-series records are strictly append-only; corrections and backfills append new Event Revisions
Backfill Reorder Window: 60-second window within which delayed out-of-order packets are re-indexed chronologically.
Device Timestamp (t_device): Device-generated epoch timestamp; the chronological ordering key.
Ingress Timestamp (t_ingress): Arrival time at the ingestion entry point; never used for ordering.
VALIDATION_FAILED: Status flag tagged on samples violating a Sensor Metric Boundary; payload is kept.
Telemetry Sample: Individual 1Hz data point of a sensor metric.
Broadcast honours downstream backpressure and does not block
Only samples already validated by Telemetry Ingestion & Validation are propagated

assumptions.status: RESOLVED (decided here; replaces the discovery Ambiguity)
assumptions.decision: Delivery is treated as at-least-once. Discriminator: natural identity (device id, metric, t_device) PLUS the sample value. Resend classes: (a) same identity and same value = retry, a no-op duplicate (no new row, no event, counted); (b) same identity and a different value = correction, appended as a new Event Revision with the next revision number, raw record untouched, TelemetryBackfillRevisionAppended published; (c) new identity = new raw record.
assumptions.invariant_owner: Telemetry Ingestion & Validation (ingestion aggregate, enforced in domain and by a unique key on identity + revision in the store)
assumptions.excludes: A client-supplied idempotency key is not used (description names none); value is part of the retry test, not part of the identity, so corrections are never silently reclassified as duplicates.

assumptions.status: RESOLVED (decided here; replaces the discovery Open question)
assumptions.decision: A packet later than the 60-second Backfill Reorder Window is never dropped: it is appended as an Event Revision flagged late, ordered by t_device, published as TelemetryBackfillRevisionAppended. Exclusion: rejection is not used because payloads are never dropped.

Telemetry Ingestion & Validation owns validation and the validation status; it alone decides VALIDATION_FAILED. Distribution trusts the published status and never revalidates: it broadcasts samples whose status is valid (ingested and revision events) and does not place TelemetrySampleValidationFailed samples in broadcast windows (it only counts them).
assumptions.invariant_owner: Telemetry Ingestion & Validation (validation); Telemetry Stream Distribution (filter on published status)

assumptions.decision: Ground contact time, respiration and swim stroke telemetry have no named range, and Swimming Pace has only the lower bound >45 sec/100m (no upper bound). No bound is invented; a metric with no configured boundary is accepted unvalidated (validation disabled) and boundaries are bound to configuration keys.
Two contexts retained as discovered (ingestion/validation and stream distribution); medium confidence.

risks: Sliding-window size and its relation to the 60-second reorder window are unspecified: window size is a configuration key with no invented default; reported as an open question to the operator
Value-less boundaries (ground contact time, respiration, swim stroke, swimming pace upper bound) leave those metrics unvalidated
At-least-once delivery assumption (A1) may mismatch real device transport; confidence low
Revisions to windows already broadcast are propagated eventually; consumers may see a window then its revision
Reordering buffer and window buffers must be bounded; unbounded buffers are forbidden, overflow policy must be planned without dropping payloads (backpressure, not drop)
Sink lifecycle: multicast fan-out sinks must use onBackpressureBuffer(capacity, false) so a subscriber disconnect cannot terminate ingestion
Log correlation across event-loop hops needs context-propagation or explicit audit passing
Ingested raw telemetry grows continuously (1Hz per metric per device): retention and partitioning is a capacity risk

drivers: append-only writes at high 1Hz multi-device throughput
non-blocking access (R2DBC compatible, no blocking I/O)
ordered reads by t_device for a device and metric
Event Revisions need a durable history that is never mutated
Telemetry Stream Distribution owns no durable state

storage_paradigm.primary: relational, append-only tables (simplest paradigm meeting ordering, uniqueness and append-only invariants; rejected: document and log stores for lack of the uniqueness and keyset-ordered range reads; revisit if measured write volume exceeds a single relational engine)
storage_paradigm.derived: Windowed buffer in distribution: in-memory transient, rebuilt from published events; staleness bounded by the window; no durable store

concepts.name: RawTelemetryRecord
concepts.key: (device_id, metric, t_device) natural identity; surrogate record id
invariants: payload never dropped, including VALIDATION_FAILED samples
concepts.sensitivity: health-related biometric data tied to a device id: classify as personal/sensitive; encrypt at rest and in transit; retention defined by operator (open question)

concepts.name: EventRevision
concepts.key: (device_id, metric, t_device, revision_number); refs the raw record by id
invariants: append-only, revision numbers strictly increase per identity
a retry with an identical value appends nothing (A1)
unique key on identity + revision_number gives optimistic concurrency under concurrent writers

concepts.name: SampleValidationStatus
concepts.key: carried on each RawTelemetryRecord and EventRevision (no separate table)
invariants: VALIDATION_FAILED tagged iff a configured Sensor Metric Boundary is violated

concepts.name: AuditEntry
concepts.sensitivity: operational; no payload values, no personal data

data_model.relationships: EventRevision references RawTelemetryRecord by id; no cross-aggregate transaction; one aggregate per transaction

queries: append raw record or revision (high frequency, write-only, no read-before-write beyond identity lookup by unique key)
lookup latest revision for an identity to classify retry vs correction (strong consistency)
keyset-ordered read by (device_id, metric, t_device) bounded page size; no offsets, no unbounded scans
persistence.performance: Non-blocking writes with backpressure; batching allowed; capacity assumptions unmeasured (open question); shard/partition only on measured volume
persistence.migration_plan: Flyway, ordered, expand-only V<n>__snake_case.sql under src/main/resources/db/migration (spring.flyway.locations: classpath:db/migration); PostgreSQL-compatible DDL portable to plain H2 (no vendor-specific types); JDBC url and R2DBC url from distinct placeholders; embedded H2 only through the test-profile document; rollback by restoring from backup, never destructive down-scripts
persistence.backup_recovery: Operator-owned periodic backup and point-in-time restore of the relational store; append-only data allows verification by revision counts; derived windows rebuilt from new events
open_questions: Retention period and archival of raw telemetry
Expected devices count and sustained write rate for capacity sizing

uncounted_failures.uncredentialed event dropped: refused at the consumer boundary; audited and logged only, no per-device counter (cardinality bound)
uncounted_failures.stream subscriber beyond cap: refused with 503; surfaced by the HTTP status, not a separate meter

uncounted_steps.packet received: counted via telemetry.ingest.samples at sample append; the receipt boundary itself is only logged
uncounted_steps.ingestion event published: delivery outcome counted by telemetry.stream.broadcast downstream
uncounted_steps.broadcast demand exhausted: log only; outcome tag on telemetry.stream.broadcast

audit_trail.port: AuditTrail (application port; append-only adapter in infrastructure)

observability.metric_tag_policy: bounded tags only (metric kind, status, outcome, reason); never device ids

export.logs: structured ECS JSON lines to a local append-only rolling file sink (logs/telemetry-ingestion-processing.log); external log collectors read the file, never the app
export.audit: append-only audit_trail table plus the same structured fields in the log file
export.metrics: Micrometer via actuator; no scrape endpoint unless the description names one
export.runtime_dependency: none on external tools; boot test passes with them absent
